A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Retro-Expert. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures and wet-lab evidence, support reliable comparison despite substantial scientific and presentation revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, expert evaluations, multi-step predictions and two wet-lab syntheses.

after.justification: v3 reports revised benchmark results and additional behavioral, ablation and expert analyses, while retaining the wet-lab results.

M1.justification: v3 introduces Chem-RM's RDKit-based structural reward and a correction-weighted nonlinear advantage calculation for KGPO (Section 3.5). These substantially revise reward modeling and optimization. Candidate selection, generation and rewards for rejecting incorrect candidates already appeared in v2, including its Figure 5.

E1.justification: USPTO-50K, USPTO-FULL, ChemBench, PaRoutes and the two wet-lab targets are retained. v3 Section 4.7 additionally reports testing 3-oxa[3.1.1]propellane and 3-aza[3.1.1]propellane as challenging targets beyond the benchmarks, providing a limited coverage extension.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-3-7-sonnet and Qwen few-shot/SFT comparison rows. Tables 2–3 add MHNReact and NAG2G. Conversely, the standalone DMS-Deep comparator in v2 Table 8 disappears from v3's multi-step comparison, although the same cited work remains the route generator under the name DMS-Model.

E3.justification: v3 introduces an expert evaluation of 500 samples across six annotation dimensions and matched-reward GRPO/KGPO controls. Multi-step evaluation adds success rate, Top-5 accuracy and inference time. T5Chem is newly evaluated with decision space, and the candidate-count sweep replaces N=7 with N=8. Dataset splits and the 9k/80k training subsets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds reward-component and matched-optimizer ablations (Tables 7 and 16), candidate-use and rejection analyses (Tables 10–11), and reasoning correctness/consistency analyses. Appendix C adds route-combination case analysis. Existing decision-space, candidate-count and positional-bias analyses are retained; selection examples are revised and reduced, while generation and failure examples largely persist.

E5.justification: v2 reports averaged expert scores without agreement estimates. v3 adds unanimous and majority inter-annotator agreement, including 83% and 98% for reasoning faithfulness (Table 13), and examines unanimously rated cases. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported Retro-Expert Top-1 accuracy changes from 70.28% to 75.69% on USPTO-50K, 49.3% to 58.4% on USPTO-FULL, and 57.00% to 65.67% on ChemBench. Explanation scores, ablation results and self-correction success also change. PaRoutes reports 41% versus v2's 38%, alongside new metrics and newly specified beam settings. These are results for the revised algorithm; wet-lab yields remain 79.3% and 58.82%.

T1.justification: v3 substantively expands the mathematical specification with a structural-feature reward, revised composite rewards, correction-weighted advantages and an explicit policy update (Section 3.5). Its reasoning trajectory also incorporates product-structure analysis and selectively used candidate dimensions. These exceed notation changes; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 withdraws v2's repeated claim to be the first retrosynthesis model generating natural-language reasoning. It refocuses the stated contributions on Chem-RM and the revised KGPO mechanism, and explicitly emphasizes efficient multi-step extension. The central interpretable collaborative-reasoning and model-compatibility claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly acknowledges chemically flawed rationales despite correct answers, limitations of the 7B backbone, and the preliminary nature of multi-step planning. v2's narrower site/path failure discussion is retained. v3 also interprets reasoning–answer alignment as causal evidence in Section 4.3, a stronger conclusion than the observational analyses establish.

D1.justification: v3 adds a source-code link, specifies multi-step beam size and route formatting, documents wet-lab case-selection criteria, and supplies revised reward weights. These extend reproducibility information, while the existing sample-curation procedure, core training configuration, prompts and detailed wet-lab procedures are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion or citations for Mol-R1, reward calibration, new comparators and propellane synthesis while retaining the related-work organization. It also replaces the chemical Retroformer reference by Wan et al. with Yao et al.'s differently titled language-agent Retroformer paper, despite retaining the numerical baseline.

P1.justification: The introduction and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten, including the exploration cold-start motivation. Interpretability evaluation is reorganized into reasoning reliability and explanation quality. The appendix is substantially reordered into Sections A–I, moving existing evaluation material earlier and separating implementation, multi-step analysis, prompts and limitations.

P2.justification: v3 consolidates and expands the LLM comparison table, adds several analysis tables, redraws the reward diagram and adopts a largely single-column appendix layout. Spectra and existing examples are resized or relocated, and selection panels are replaced or removed. Caption errors are introduced: Figure 11 labels the retained deprotection example as oxidation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens component attribution through matched reward/optimizer ablations and makes reasoning assessment more transparent through a specified expert study of 500 samples with agreement reporting. Expanded baselines and explicit limitations further improve scrutiny of the central claims. Causal faithfulness remains unproven, and the removed DMS-Deep comparison plus citation/caption errors weaken parts of the revision, but the overall gains in controlled validation and methodological specification are substantial.
